subject: GPU pool throughput scenarios & pricing path for DataWave
messages:
From: Sophia Lane <sophia.lane@datawave.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DataWave load-test export + ask about reserved sizing and discounts

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a couple of sustained load passes against the hosted endpoint to approximate what dedicated throughput would look like for our peak periods. Attached are: a CSV export (tps_dashboard_q1.csv) and a small trace sample (trace_sample_0207.json). High level:

- 95th percentile sustained QPS per-hour: 1,850 requests/sec (average token length ~140)
- Peak 5-minute spikes hit ~2,900 r/s during a campaign 
- Typical conversational latency target for users: ≤ 350ms p95

We want Redwood Dedicated pricing and sizing guidance for a pool that covers our baseline 2k r/s with 30% headroom for spikes, plus a lower-cost warm pool for overflow. Specifically:

1) Target committed pool sizing scenarios (3 sizing options)
2) Estimates of p50/p95 latency for each option under our load mix
3) Pricing bands and discount guidance for a 12/24/36 month reserved commit
4) Any suggested burst/overflow strategies (regional fallback, cheaper model variants)

Can you share an initial proposal by EOD Tuesday (9th)? Procurement will need a rough MRR and expected utilization numbers to evaluate.

Appreciate it — Sophia
Senior Infrastructure Lead
DataWave AI

Attachments: tps_dashboard_q1.csv (CSV), trace_sample_0207.json (JSON)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sophia Lane <sophia.lane@datawave.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DataWave load-test export + ask about reserved sizing and discounts

Sophia —

Received, thanks for the exports. Quick clarifying q's to make our sizing assumptions align with yours:

- Is the 95th percentile sustained number (1,850 r/s) measured across a single region or global aggregated traffic?
- Are the spikes you saw tied to a single campaign window (i.e., all traffic to one region), or split?
- Do you need multi-region active/active at launch or is single-region with failover acceptable?

Vivek will review the traces and produce three concrete pool-size scenarios (conservative / balanced / aggressive) with rough latency estimates and impact on cost. We’ll include recommended overflow strategies (warm pool, model variants, and burst fallback). Expect a preliminary worksheet by EOD Tuesday.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: DataWave load-test export + ask about reserved sizing and discounts

Team / Sophia —

I pulled the CSV and sample traces and ran them through our sizing model. Summary of the three scenarios attached as a quick sheet (redwood_proposal_gpu3.xlsx). Key assumptions: tokenization and average prompt+reply token count ~ 140, batching efficiency 1.8x at 200ms batching window, KV cache hit rate 12% for repeated contexts.

Scenario A — Conservative (target sustained 1,900 r/s, 30% headroom):
- GPU pool: 12 x A100-equivalent serving nodes
- Expected p95 latency: ~340–360ms (model variant: rw-medium-4096-q8)
- Estimated committed throughput utilization: 65–75%
- Monthly Opex proxy (uncommitted rate equivalent): baseline cost band 8.4k token-units/hr

Scenario B — Balanced (target sustained 2,500 r/s, 30% headroom for spikes):
- GPU pool: 16 x A100-equivalent serving nodes
- Expected p95 latency: ~300–330ms (model variant: rw-large-8192-q8)
- Estimated committed utilization: 72–82%
- Monthly Opex proxy: baseline cost band 11.2k token-units/hr

Scenario C — Aggressive (target sustained 3,200 r/s with room for growth / peak campaigns):
- GPU pool: 22 x A100-equivalent serving nodes
- Expected p95 latency: ~260–290ms (model variant: rw-large-8192 + KV-prefetch)
- Estimated committed utilization: 78–88%
- Monthly Opex proxy: baseline cost band 15.6k token-units/hr

Overflow suggestions:
- Warm overflow pool (lower-cost instance type) sized to absorb 25% of peak spikes with automatic burst to regionally-fallback cheaper model variant.
- Configure prefix caching for repeated conversation starters (we saw ~6–8% gains in token reduction for similar traces).

I’ve flagged the utilization bands to Ben for discount guidance (will need to map to a commit tier matrix). Sophia, I also attached an example p95 latency trace for Scenario B and the dashboard link so you can inspect traces live.

Attachments: redwood_proposal_gpu3.xlsx
Redwood dashboard: https://app.redwood.example.com/dashboards/DW-TPs-2027

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Sophia Lane <sophia.lane@datawave.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DataWave load-test export + ask about reserved sizing and discounts

Hannah / Vivek / Sophia —

Thanks for the scenarios, Vivek — clean work. Pricing guidance (ballpark, subject to legal/finance review):

Commit tiers (per-month committed spend, illustrative):
- 12-month commit: base price P, eligible for 8% discount off hosted per-token list (plus 2% additional for upfront payment)
- 24-month commit: base price 0.93P, eligible for 13% discount (plus 3% upfront)
- 36-month commit: base price 0.88P, eligible for 18% discount (plus 4% upfront)

For the three scenarios: map utilization bands to tiered unit prices and propose the following starting negotiation posture:
- Scenario A: propose 12-month commit at 75% utilization target; offer a 10% volume rebate if actual utilization > 85% for two consecutive months.
- Scenario B: propose 24-month commit, 15% discount, include one month of burst credits per quarter (limited to 20% of committed capacity).
- Scenario C: propose 36-month commit, 18% discount, add an SLA-backed latency target (p95 <= 300ms) with a small credit schedule for missed SLOs.

A few commercial caveats:
- Discounts are tied to committed MRR and minimum utilization reserves; finance will need the exact committed quantity to finalize.
- We can include a 60-day proof window with reduced charge while DataWave performs an in-market verification run (helps mitigate commercial risk).

If Sophia is comfortable, I can draft the priced term sheet for the Scenario B 24-month posture to accelerate Procurement review.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sophia Lane <sophia.lane@datawave.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: GPU pool throughput scenarios & pricing path for DataWave

Sophia — quick next steps and mutual action plan (MAP):

1) We propose moving forward with Scenario B (balanced) as the recommended starter. Ben will produce a priced term sheet for a 24-month commit that includes the 15% discount and quarterly burst credits. (Ben ETA: EOD Friday)
2) DataWave signs a short TAP (trial activation period) for 60 days during which you run the in-market verification; costs discounted per Ben’s note.
3) Redwood will enable a warm overflow pool and the KV caching policy to replicate the test environment. Vivek will own the runbook for the verification runs.
4) Procurement: if the term sheet looks good, we’ll route to legal and finance; please identify any special procurement clauses up front.

I’ve attached a draft MAP and the small worksheet we used. I’ll follow up with a DocuSign link for the TAP when Ben shares the priced term sheet.

Appreciate the partnership — looking forward to getting you onto Dedicated.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
